passage:
The old bridge over Silver River was too narrow for cars, so the city built a new one beside it. Many people thought the old bridge would be removed.
But local residents asked the city to keep it for walkers and bikes. They said the bridge was part of their memories. Children had crossed it to school. Couples had taken wedding photos there. Farmers had carried vegetables across it in the morning.
The city repaired the bridge and added lights. Now people walk there in the evening, watching the river below.
The old bridge no longer does its first job, but it still connects people. Sometimes usefulness changes with time, but it does not always disappear.
